faq.a: Khalimat is associated with the Arabic form خَلِيمَة, whose core sense is khalimat; halima (caucasian form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Khalimat?
faq.a: Khalimat is associated with Arabic. Khalimat is the Caucasian form of Arabic حَلِيمَة (Ḥalīma), meaning 'forbearing'.
Yes — the underlying form خَلِيمَة is Arabic.
Khalimat can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Khalimat should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ḥalīma is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Khalimat mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Khalimat is rendered حلیمه and carries the sense حلیمه، بردبار.
A romanized syllable approximation is kha-li-mat. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Khalimat?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Khalimat, khalimat. Script forms are حلیمه, خليمه, خلیمہ, خَلِيمَة, ख़लीमात.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
